Public Participation GIS & Spatial Analysis

The challenge

Determine the spatial conflict between social use areas and flying squirrel habitats across three municipalities in Finland. The analysis needed to quantify overlap at multiple scales and verify results statistically — a complex multi-method problem with real conservation implications.

The approach

Used ArcGIS Desktop for spatial data analysis — applying Getis-Ord hotspot analysis and Kernel Density Estimation to identify clustering patterns. R was used for statistical verification using phi coefficient and Bhattacharyya distance. Data was gathered through Public Participation GIS (PPGIS), engaging local stakeholders to map social use areas that would otherwise be invisible to conventional data collection.

Key outcomes

Spatial conflict mapped across 3 municipalities using hotspot and kernel density analysis

PPGIS methodology engaged stakeholders to capture social land-use data at scale

Statistical verification confirmed spatial findings using phi coefficient and Bhattacharyya distance

To learn more visit LUKE's official project page: flying-squirrel-life.
